purpose: Small synthetic validation of the slide design, diagram writing, repair, and semantic verification paths. No user library data was used.

evidence.title: Synthetic review procedure
evidence.text: In this synthetic example procedure, review the evidence first. If the required information is complete, prepare a recommendation. If required information is missing, request the missing material. These are conditional alternatives, not a sequence through both outcomes.

verifiedSlide:
<!-- layout: diagram -->
## Missing information changes the next step

In this synthetic example procedure, both arrows leave the same review step and only one outcome applies at a time [1]. The condition on each arrow is whether the required information is complete or missing [1].

| From | Relationship | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Review the evidence | if complete [1] | Prepare a recommendation |
| Review the evidence | if missing [1] | Request missing material |

Note: Start by pointing at the single left-hand node, "Review the evidence" — this is the synthetic example procedure from the previous slide, and every path starts here [1]. Then trace the two separate arrows: one leaves the review when the required information is complete and leads to preparing a recommendation; the other leaves the same review when required information is missing and leads to requesting the missing material [1]. Say plainly that "conditional" means only one of these applies at a time — the source calls them conditional alternatives, not a sequence through both outcomes [1]. Pause after that, so the two arrows are read side by side rather than as step one and step two. The sources do not say what happens after a request for missing material, so do not sketch a third step. Transition: the next slide gives one illustrative training result from this procedure.
